req.title: Posts include author username
req.statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET / joins post rows with users and returns the author's username in the response. Tests must verify: (1) positive — the index page returns HTTP 200 and contains known author usernames from the pre-loaded data; (2) negative — a response without the JOIN would lack usernames, so we assert exact username strings are present; (3) boundary — the most-recent post (id=20, author_id=1, username='Rahul') appears first due to ORDER BY created DESC, and the oldest post (id=8, author_id=1, created 2024-11-03) appears last, verifying ordering and join correctness at both ends. Additional tests cover multiple distinct authors and the exact SQL join fields (id, title, body, created, author_id, username) to kill mutations that remove the JOIN clause or swap column references.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_with_author_username
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with 5 users and 20 posts
Post id=20 authored by user id=1 (Rahul)
Post id=7 authored by user id=2 (Anjali)
actions: Create Flask test app with temp database
trace: R-FLASKR-024: index response includes author username via JOIN
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_returns_200_with_author_username():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data

test_index_returns_200_with_author_username()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')

tests.name: test_index_username_matches_correct_post
preconditions: Post id=17 authored by user id=3 (Ishaan), title 'Pertex vertex vertex'
Post id=14 authored by user id=2 (Anjali), title 'Oova alpha orbit'
JOIN must associate correct username to each post
actions: Create Flask test app with temp database
Verify Ishaan and Anjali appear (their posts exist); verify ordering places Ishaan post after Anjali post by date
expected: Post title 'Pertex vertex vertex' (2025-02-04) appears after 'Zeacon signal prism' (2025-01-03) — ORDER BY DESC
trace: R-FLASKR-024: correct username-to-post mapping via JOIN; ordering mutation detection
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_username_matches_correct_post():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    html = r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in html
    assert b'Anjali' in html
    assert b'Pertex vertex vertex' in html
    assert b'Zeacon signal prism' in html
    # Pertex (2025-02-04) is newer than Zeacon (2025-01-03), so appears first
    idx_pertex = html.find(b'Pertex vertex vertex')
    idx_zeacon = html.find(b'Zeacon signal prism')
    assert idx_pertex < idx_zeacon
